title: The difficulty: no one resists God's will, so freedom and the will's indetermination seem lost
source_text: II. Inde autem omnino perire videtur libertas, tam in Angelis quam in hominibus. Nec enim ullus divinae voluntati resistere potest. Adeoque si Deus vult Angelos & homines id agere quod agunt, aliter agere non possunt, & sic libere non agunt, nec sunt actuum suorum Domini. Deinde si voluntatis humanae actiones immutabilibus Dei decretis determinatae sunt, tolli videtur omnis voluntatis indeterminatio, & in agendo indifferentia, in qua ratio libertatis consistit.
pass_a_gloss: II. But from this freedom seems to perish altogether, as much in Angels as in men. For no one can resist the divine will. And so if God wills that Angels and men do what they do, they cannot do otherwise, and so they do not act freely, nor are they lords of their own acts. Then if the actions of the human will are determined by immutable decrees of God, all indetermination of the will seems to be taken away, and the indifference in acting, in which the nature of freedom consists.
pass_b_english: Yet this seems to destroy freedom entirely, in angels and in men alike. No one can resist God's will. If God wills that angels and men do what they do, they cannot act otherwise; so they do not act freely and are not masters of their own acts.

Again, if the actions of the human will are determined by God's unchangeable decrees, the will seems to lose all indetermination, and with it the indifference in acting in which the essence of freedom consists.

choices.why: The will's openness to either alternative, in which many placed the essence of freedom; kept as the technical term.
